## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater euglenoid characterized by a rigid green cell that is distinctly twisted or helically contorted, with the broadest portion near the middle and a long, narrow tail extending from the posterior end. Phacus tortus has longitudinally striated pellicle markings that follow the cell’s twisted shape and usually contains a prominent central paramylon body used for carbohydrate storage. It occurs in freshwater habitats including ponds, lakes, ditches, swamps, and other standing or slow-moving waters. Like other photosynthetic Phacus, it contributes to primary production and forms part of the microbial plankton community.
